program.name: Engineering Program, A.S.
program.minGrade: A grade of C or higher is required in all career studies courses, and in any course that is a prerequisite for another.

hero.title: Plan the route from your first class to your engineering degree.
hero.sub: Pick a discipline, look at the work engineers do, then build the semester plan and transfer plan that get you to a bachelor's degree. Bring the finished plan to your advising appointment at Brookdale.
hero.goalDone: Your plan is ready for advising.
hero.goalTodo: Finish the steps to complete your plan.

steps.title: Choose your engineering discipline
steps.intro: Brookdale's Engineering A.S. has five major areas of study. Your first semester is the same for all of them, and you declare your area near the end of ENGI 105, so it is fine to start with a best guess.

steps.title: Choose 3 to 6 careers that interest you
steps.intro: These are kinds of work engineers do after a bachelor's degree. Pick the ones that sound like work you'd enjoy. Highlighted cards fit the discipline you chose in step 1.

steps.title: Build your semester-by-semester plan
steps.intro: This is the catalog's suggested sequence for your discipline. Check off classes you've passed, and move a class to a different term if you need a lighter load. The planner checks prerequisites and which terms each class runs.

steps.title: Plan your transfer to a four-year school
steps.intro: This degree parallels the first two years of a four-year engineering program, and most engineering jobs require the bachelor's degree. Choose the schools you're considering so you can check how each class transfers.

steps.title: Plan experience outside the classroom
steps.intro: Internships, research, and project teams help you choose a discipline and strengthen a transfer application.

steps.title: Review, save, and print
steps.intro: This is the plan you'll bring to advising. Save it to keep working later, print it, or download a copy.

tracks.name: Chemical Engineering
tracks.desc: Design the processes that turn raw materials into fuels, medicines, food, and plastics. Heaviest in chemistry: two semesters of organic.

tracks.name: Civil Engineering
tracks.desc: Design and build roads, bridges, buildings, and water systems. Built on statics, dynamics, and strength of materials.

tracks.name: Electrical Engineering
tracks.desc: Design circuits, electronics, power, and digital systems. Adds circuits, electronics, digital logic, and a third semester of physics.

tracks.name: Industrial Engineering
tracks.desc: Make factories, hospitals, and supply chains work better. At Brookdale it shares its technical electives with Civil Engineering.

tracks.name: Mechanical Engineering
tracks.desc: Design machines, engines, robots, and thermal systems. Adds dynamics, materials, and kinematics of machinery.

trackNote: Not sure? Every discipline takes the same first semester. Use ENGI 105 to explore, then come back and choose.

ECON107.preText: Foundational studies requirements in computation, reading, and writing

CHEM101.preText: High school chemistry or CHEM 100 (C or higher), and MATH 151 (C or higher)

HUM.phNote: Your choice from the Humanities list. One of your two electives is recommended from the Cultural and Global Awareness knowledge area.

HUMSS.phNote: Your choice from the Humanities or Social Sciences lists. One of your two electives is recommended from the Cultural and Global Awareness knowledge area.

topics: Equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies

ENGI105.note: Take this in your first term. You declare your major area of study near the end of the course.

topics: Planar kinetics of a rigid body
Design and deflection of beams and shafts

waive.note: The catalog lists MATH 171 as a prerequisite for PHYS 121, but its suggested sequence puts both in the same term. Confirm with your advisor that you can take them together.

The catalog's suggested sequence shows a summer technical elective after year one, but the ENGI 216 course page lists ENGI 102 (a Spring, year-two class) as a prerequisite. Confirm with your advisor when to take ENGI 216.

entry: MATH 171 Calculus I requires MATH 153 or equivalent. If your placement is below calculus, you will need one or more math classes first, and the plan below will take longer.
CHEM 101 requires high school chemistry (or CHEM 100) and MATH 151.

advice.text: ENGI 216 runs only in Summer II. Ask your advisor which summer to take it, since its course page lists ENGI 102 as a prerequisite.

In this discipline the catalog sequence leaves fall of year two light and spring of year two heavy, because ENGI 102, 205, and 206 all run only in Spring. Ask your advisor about moving ECON 107 or an elective into the fall.
Electrical Engineering does not require CHEM 102. Your Humanities or Social Sciences elective takes its place in spring of year one.
Organic Chemistry I and II must be taken in order across your second year. A late start in chemistry pushes both back.

more.label: Occupational Outlook Handbook: architecture and engineering

list.name: Process engineer
list.desc: Designs and improves the equipment and steps used to make chemicals, fuels, or food at scale.

list.name: Pharmaceutical or biotech engineer
list.desc: Scales up the manufacture of medicines and biological products and keeps production within strict quality rules.

list.name: Materials engineer
list.desc: Develops and tests metals, polymers, ceramics, and composites for a specific job.

list.name: Environmental engineer
list.desc: Designs systems that clean water and air, manage waste, and clean up contaminated sites.

list.name: Structural engineer
list.desc: Designs the frames of buildings and bridges so they carry their loads safely.

list.name: Transportation engineer
list.desc: Plans and designs roads, rail, airports, and traffic systems.

list.name: Geotechnical engineer
list.desc: Studies soil and rock so foundations, tunnels, and retaining walls stay put.

list.name: Water resources engineer
list.desc: Designs water supply, stormwater, and flood control systems.

list.name: Construction project engineer
list.desc: Turns design drawings into a built project on schedule and on budget.

list.name: Industrial engineer
list.desc: Studies how people, machines, and materials move through a workplace and redesigns the system to waste less.

list.name: Quality engineer
list.desc: Sets up the tests and statistics that keep products within specification.

list.name: Supply chain or logistics engineer
list.desc: Designs how goods are stored, routed, and delivered.

list.name: Manufacturing engineer
list.desc: Designs production lines, tooling, and the steps used to build a product.

list.name: Electronics design engineer
list.desc: Designs circuit boards and electronic devices, from sensors to consumer products.

list.name: Power systems engineer
list.desc: Designs and operates the generation, transmission, and distribution of electricity.

list.name: Embedded systems or computer hardware engineer
list.desc: Builds the processors and firmware inside cars, appliances, and medical devices.

list.name: Telecommunications or RF engineer
list.desc: Designs wireless, fiber, and antenna systems that carry voice and data.

list.name: Controls and automation engineer
list.desc: Programs the sensors, motors, and controllers that run machines and plants.

list.name: Mechanical design engineer
list.desc: Designs parts and assemblies in CAD, then analyzes and tests them.

list.name: HVAC or building systems engineer
list.desc: Designs heating, cooling, and ventilation for buildings.

list.name: Aerospace engineer
list.desc: Designs and tests aircraft, spacecraft, and their propulsion systems.

list.name: Automotive engineer
list.desc: Designs vehicle systems such as powertrains, suspensions, and safety equipment.

list.name: Robotics engineer
list.desc: Combines mechanics, electronics, and software to build robots and automated machines.

list.name: Biomedical device engineer
list.desc: Designs implants, instruments, and diagnostic equipment for health care.

transfer.tip: Requirements differ by school and by major. An individual's program may vary depending on the transfer school, so choose your electives with your target school's requirements in front of you.
transfer.noNote: This degree is designed for transfer, and most engineering jobs require a bachelor's degree. If you don't plan to transfer, ask your advisor whether a different program fits your goal better.

types: Summer research program at a university
experience.callout: Good to know: licensed Professional Engineers (PEs) usually start by passing the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) exam near the end of an accredited bachelor's program. Licensure matters most in civil engineering. You don't need to act on this yet.
experience.yesSub: I want experience before I transfer
experience.noNote: Experience outside class strengthens a transfer application. If an internship won't fit, ask about an engineering club or a short research project.

partNote: You plan to attend part-time. Keep the math and physics sequences moving, because most engineering classes depend on them.
